For everyone

Runbook

How to install, test and run DT-GSK (the proposed Dimension-Tiered Gaining-Sharing Knowledge algorithm) and the six GSK-family algorithms it is compared with, on five CEC benchmark suites.

If you want toRead
Install, test and run the algorithms, and compare their resultsPart 1 (about 30 minutes to a first result, most of it installing and testing)
Rebuild the paper, run the revision experiments, or run the release gatesPart 2

Part 1. Run and test DT-GSK

Type every command in a terminal, inside the project folder (the folder that contains run.py). The commands are the same on Windows, Linux and macOS unless a step says otherwise.

Step 1. Get the code

You need Git (on Windows, install "Git for Windows" from git-scm.com).

git clone https://github.com/MostafaMassoud/DT-GSK.git
cd DT-GSK

On Windows, clone into a short folder (for example, type cd C:\ before the two commands above), because some file paths in the repository are long. The download is about 340 MB, and the folder then needs about 1.7 GB of disk space, mostly for the paper's published results, which Step 6 uses; the Python environment of Step 2 adds about 0.6 GB.

Step 2. Install Python and the requirements

Use Python 3.10 (64-bit). All of the paper's results were produced with Python 3.10.11; on Windows, use the 64-bit Windows installer of Python 3.10.11 from python.org. Python 3.11 to 3.13 are accepted but were not tested, and Python 3.14 is not supported. MATLAB and a C compiler are not needed.

Create a virtual environment inside the project folder and activate it.

Windows (Command Prompt or PowerShell):

py -3.10 -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate

If PowerShell says that running scripts is disabled, run this line and then the activate line again (it affects only that window):

Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass

Linux or macOS:

python3.10 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

The prompt now starts with (.venv). Then, on every system:

python --version
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"

python --version should print Python 3.10.x. The install downloads a few hundred MB and can take several minutes; wait for the line that starts with Successfully installed. It installs NumPy, SciPy, pandas, matplotlib, PyYAML and Numba, the commands gsk-run, gsk-list, gsk-stats and gsk-validate, and the test tools.

Every new terminal window: go to the project folder and activate the environment again (.venv\Scripts\activate on Windows, source .venv/bin/activate on Linux or macOS) before running anything below.

Step 3. Test the code

A quick check (about five to ten minutes the first time, while Numba compiles; faster later):

python -m pytest -q tests/smoke

The full test suite (allow ten minutes or more the first time, while Numba compiles its kernels; later runs are faster):

python -m pytest -q

Both should end with a line that says passed and no failed. Both also report a few warnings (a UserWarning about linkage_block_size_by_dim), and the full suite reports 2 skipped; all of these are expected.

Step 4. Run your first experiment

DT-GSK on one CEC2017 function, with a deliberately tiny budget:

python run.py --root . --optimizer dt-gsk --suite cec2017 --function 1 --dimension 10 --runs 1 --max-evaluations 2000 --output-root test_results
  • The first run can pause for a minute or two while Numba compiles, both before and after it prints its settings. Later runs start in seconds.
  • Near the end it prints PASS DT-GSK. A little above that, a "Mean Comparison" table compares the test with the paper's result: its Status column shows v, and the Summary line under it ends with v Worse: 1. That is expected, because the test uses 2,000 evaluations instead of the full budget of 100,000.
  • Keep test runs in their own folder (here test_results), never in your real results folder. A run skips every run it already finds in its folder, whatever budget produced it, so a short test left there would be kept as if it were a real result.

Step 5. Run the algorithms on a benchmark suite

run.py is the only script you need. Its settings are command-line options:

OptionMeaning
--optimizergsk, agsk, apgsk, fdb-agsk, atmals-gsk, egsk or dt-gsk; several are separated by commas
--suitecec2011, cec2013, cec2013lsgo, cec2017 or cec2020
--functionthe functions to run, for example 1:30 (a range) or 1,3,5
--dimensionthe dimensions, for example 10,30,50,100; native for CEC2011 and CEC2013LSGO, where each problem has its own fixed dimension
--runsindependent runs per function and dimension; always give it, because the default is 1
--parallel --workers 4runs 4 runs at the same time (without it, only 2); raise it to use more of your CPU cores, see Use more CPU cores to run faster
--numba-threads 1one thread per job, as in the paper; keep it
--output-root my_resultsthe folder where your results are written

The evaluation budget of each suite (for example 10000 x D for CEC2017) and the random seeds are set automatically to the paper's protocol, so do not add --max-evaluations to a real run.

The paper's settings, all seven algorithms in one command per suite:

CEC2017: functions 1 to 30 (F2 is left out automatically, as in the paper), D = 10, 30, 50, 100, 51 runs.

python run.py --root . --optimizer gsk,agsk,apgsk,fdb-agsk,atmals-gsk,egsk,dt-gsk --suite cec2017 --function 1:30 --dimension 10,30,50,100 --runs 51 --parallel --workers 4 --numba-threads 1 --output-root my_results

CEC2011: 22 real-world problems, each at its own fixed dimension, 25 runs.

python run.py --root . --optimizer gsk,agsk,apgsk,fdb-agsk,atmals-gsk,egsk,dt-gsk --suite cec2011 --function 1:22 --dimension native --runs 25 --parallel --workers 4 --numba-threads 1 --output-root my_results

CEC2013: 28 functions, D = 10, 30, 50, 51 runs.

python run.py --root . --optimizer gsk,agsk,apgsk,fdb-agsk,atmals-gsk,egsk,dt-gsk --suite cec2013 --function 1:28 --dimension 10,30,50 --runs 51 --parallel --workers 4 --numba-threads 1 --output-root my_results

CEC2020: 10 functions, D = 5, 10, 15, 20, 30 runs (F6 and F7 are not defined at D = 5 and are skipped there automatically, as in the paper).

python run.py --root . --optimizer gsk,agsk,apgsk,fdb-agsk,atmals-gsk,egsk,dt-gsk --suite cec2020 --function 1:10 --dimension 5,10,15,20 --runs 30 --parallel --workers 4 --numba-threads 1 --output-root my_results

CEC2013LSGO: 15 functions at D = 1000 (F13 and F14 at D = 905), 25 runs. Two commands: the first runs the six other algorithms, the second runs DT-GSK with its own settings file. Always run DT-GSK on this suite with the second command only; added to the first, it would run with the wrong settings.

python run.py --root . --optimizer gsk,agsk,apgsk,fdb-agsk,atmals-gsk,egsk --suite cec2013lsgo --function 1:15 --dimension native --runs 25 --parallel --workers 2 --numba-threads 1 --output-root my_results
python run.py --root . --config configs/dtgsk_cec2013lsgo.yml --workers 2 --output-root my_results

Good to know:

  • One algorithm only: put a single name after --optimizer, for example --optimizer dt-gsk.
  • A smaller part: change the values already in the command, for example --dimension 10,30,50,100 to --dimension 10. Do not add a second --dimension, --function or --optimizer at the end: repeated options are added together, not replaced. For CEC2017, F2 is left out automatically only with exactly 1:30; for a smaller set leave it out yourself, for example --function 1,3:10.
  • If a run stops (a crash, a reboot, Ctrl-C), type the same command again: finished runs are kept and only the missing ones run. Do not add --overwrite, which deletes the algorithm's earlier results for that suite in the folder.

Closest match to the paper at D = 50 and above. In the same terminal, before the run.py command, set six thread variables to 1:

Windows PowerShell:

$env:OMP_NUM_THREADS=1; $env:MKL_NUM_THREADS=1; $env:OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1; $env:VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1; $env:NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=1; $env:NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=1

Linux or macOS:

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1 NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=1 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=1

In Command Prompt, type set OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, then the same set line for each of MKL_NUM_THREADS, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS, NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS and NUMBA_NUM_THREADS.

Use more CPU cores to run faster

The commands above use --workers 4, so four runs go at the same time (without --workers, the program uses only 2). If your computer has more cores, raise this number and the run finishes sooner. The results stay exactly the same, as long as --numba-threads 1 is kept: each run's random seed depends only on the function, the dimension and the run number, never on how many workers there are.

1. Find how many cores your computer has (this works on every system):

python -c "import os; print(os.cpu_count())"

Other ways: echo %NUMBER_OF_PROCESSORS% in Command Prompt, $env:NUMBER_OF_PROCESSORS in PowerShell, nproc on Linux, and sysctl -n hw.ncpu on macOS.

2. Choose the number of workers:

  • Start from your number of cores minus 2, so the computer stays responsive for other work.
  • Do not go above the number of runs per function (51 for CEC2017 and CEC2013, 30 for CEC2020, 25 for CEC2011 and CEC2013LSGO). The program finishes all runs of one function before it starts the next, so extra workers would only wait.
  • Some numbers use the cores better than their neighbours, because the runs of each function are shared out in rounds: for 51 runs choose 13, 17 or 26 workers; for 30 runs, 10 or 15; for 25 runs, 9 or 13. For example, 14 to 16 workers are no faster than 13 on CEC2017.
  • Each worker is a separate program that needs its own memory, so make sure the computer has memory to spare, above all on CEC2013LSGO (about 2 GB per worker). If a run ends with WARN <ALGORITHM> failed=N, lower --workers and run the same command again; only the missing runs are repeated.

3. Put your number after --workers. For example, on a computer with 16 cores (16 minus 2 is 14, and for the 51 runs of CEC2017, 13 workers are as fast as 14):

python run.py --root . --optimizer gsk,agsk,apgsk,fdb-agsk,atmals-gsk,egsk,dt-gsk --suite cec2017 --function 1:30 --dimension 10,30,50,100 --runs 51 --parallel --workers 13 --numba-threads 1 --output-root my_results

Full runs take a long time. Approximate time for all seven algorithms together, measured on the authors' 22-core computer (yours may be slower):

SuiteCPU-hoursWith the workers shown above (4; 2 for CEC2013LSGO)With 13 to 15 workers, as in the paper
CEC2011about 65about 16 hoursabout 5 hours
CEC2013about 105about 1 dayabout 7 hours
CEC2017about 260about 3 daysabout 1 day
CEC2020about 260about 3 daysabout 20 hours
CEC2013LSGOabout 960about 20 daysabout 3 days with 13 workers, if the computer has about 32 GB of memory

Step 6. Compare the algorithms

The comparison from the paper's published results (nothing to run first):

gsk-stats --suite cec2017 --out comparison/cec2017
gsk-stats --suite cec2011 --out comparison/cec2011
gsk-stats --suite cec2013 --out comparison/cec2013
gsk-stats --suite cec2020 --out comparison/cec2020
gsk-stats --suite cec2013lsgo --out comparison/cec2013lsgo

Each command writes, into the folder after --out, a text report (<suite>_statistical_report.txt) with the Friedman mean ranks of the seven algorithms and, for DT-GSK against each other algorithm, the Wilcoxon signed-rank test and the win/tie/loss counts; a CSV of the ranks; two LaTeX tables; and figures. The p-values in the text report are not corrected for multiple comparisons; the Holm-corrected ones are in <suite>_wilcoxon_summary.tex. The CEC2011 results are labelled D0, meaning each problem at its own dimension.

gsk-stats is a convenience tool, so its numbers are close to the paper's but not always identical: it uses a simpler rule for tied pairs in the Wilcoxon test, and on CEC2013LSGO it ranks the 13 functions at D = 1000, while the paper pools all 15. So a few Wilcoxon decisions differ (for example CEC2013 at D = 50, where gsk-stats shows three DT-GSK wins that the paper reports as ties). The exact statistics reported in the paper are in the files friedman_ranks_*.csv and wilcoxon_holm_*.csv, in the suite's subfolder (for example cec2017/) of these folders under papers/analysis/: rel-2026-07-20-67d9345f9/ (CEC2011, CEC2013, CEC2017), cec2020-rel-2026-07-29-5867abe1e/ and lsgo-rel-2026-07-28-ff1a046ef/.

Including your own runs. gsk-stats reads the published results first, so your runs are not used by the commands above. Collect them into a panel folder first; your files replace the published ones for the same algorithm and dimension, and everything you did not run keeps its published result:

python scripts/build_stats_panel.py --suite cec2017 --results my_results --out my_panel
gsk-stats --suite cec2017 --reference-root my_panel --out comparison_mine/cec2017

For another suite, replace cec2017 everywhere in both lines. Wait until each dimension you ran has finished for all functions (the script warns about a partial file, and about a run with fewer runs or a smaller budget than the published one), and compare comparison_mine with comparison, not with the tables in the paper.

Step 7. Find your results

Each algorithm writes to my_results/<algorithm>/<suite>/summary/:

FileContents
per_run.csvone row per run: function, dimension, run, seed, best fitness, error, evaluations used and runtime
<algorithm>_<suite>_D<d>.csvthe Best, Median, Mean, Worst and SD of each function's error at dimension d (CEC2011 and CEC2013LSGO: of the objective value, so the error column of per_run.csv is NaN there; CEC2011 also writes <algorithm>_cec2011.csv, every problem you ran in one table)
run_config.json, environment.jsonthe exact settings and software versions of the run

Convergence curves are in my_results/<algorithm>/<suite>/curves/. The paper's own result for every run of every algorithm is in benchmarks/cec_reference_results/<suite>/<algorithm>/per_run.csv.

Troubleshooting

ProblemWhat to do
'git' is not recognizedInstall Git (Step 1) and open a new terminal.
Filename too long while cloning (Windows)Clone into a short folder such as C:\DT-GSK, or run git config --global core.longpaths true first.
'python' is not recognized, or the wrong versionOn Windows use py -3.10 as in Step 2; py --list shows the installed versions.
python3.10: command not found (Linux or macOS)Install Python 3.10 (Ubuntu: sudo add-apt-repository ppa:deadsnakes/ppa, then sudo apt install python3.10 python3.10-venv; macOS: the python.org installer; anywhere: pyenv), or use your system python3 if python3 --version shows 3.11 to 3.13 (accepted, not tested). Then repeat Step 2.
ensurepip is not available when creating the environment (Debian or Ubuntu)Install the venv module for that Python, for example sudo apt install python3.10-venv (or python3.12-venv), delete the .venv folder, and repeat Step 2.
running scripts is disabled on this system (PowerShell)Run Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass, then activate again; or use Command Prompt.
No module named 'gsk_family', or gsk-stats is not recognizedThe environment is not active in this window: activate it (Step 2). If it still fails, run python -m pip install -e ".[dev]" again.
A run pauses for a minute or more after it starts, or after it prints its settingsNumba is compiling its kernels once; wait.
The "Mean Comparison" table shows v and Worse after a short testExpected when --max-evaluations cuts the budget.
A run ends with WARN <ALGORITHM> failed=N instead of PASS (often a memory error, for example on CEC2013LSGO)Lower --workers and run the same command again; only the missing runs are repeated.
gsk-stats says reference directory not foundIf the message lists the suites it found, fix the spelling after --suite. Otherwise the published results are missing: use a full clone (Step 1), and run the command from the project folder.
For maintainers

Part 2. Maintainer and paper-pipeline reference

The rest of this runbook is the terse copy-paste reference behind the paper: the revision experiments, the complete data-to-PDF pipeline, the release gates and the freeze cycle, plus advanced run variants. Everything in Part 1 still applies. Run everything from the repository root (the folder that contains run.py, pyproject.toml, and src/gsk_family/); every command passes --root ., so it is portable regardless of where the checkout lives on disk.

For the narrative version of these commands -- with rationale, defaults, the console-output contract, and the parallel-backend guide -- see README.md. The two documents are kept consistent; this runbook is the terse copy-paste companion.

Optimizers (7 runnable): gsk, agsk, apgsk, fdb-agsk, atmals-gsk, dt-gsk (the proposed Dimension-Tiered Gaining-Sharing Knowledge), and egsk. egsk is a runnable optimizer ID, but its statistical-panel cells still come from the committed reference data under benchmarks/cec_reference_results/. Suites (6): cec2017, cec2011, cec2020, cec2013, cec2013lsgo, sphere.

Discover Before You Run

# Full CLI help (every flag, with defaults)
python run.py --root . --help

# What optimizers, benchmarks, and reference evidence are available
gsk-list --optimizers --benchmarks --references benchmarks/cec_reference_results

gsk-list is installed by the editable install (pip install -e .). From a plain pip checkout, run $env:PYTHONPATH = "src" in the shell first and then call python -m gsk_family.cli.list instead (see Setup).

Setup

Editable install with the dev extra (enables the gsk-* console scripts plus test, lint, and docs tooling), then run the test suite:

python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
python -m pytest -q

Plain pip instead (libraries only, no editable package, so no gsk-* scripts). python run.py and scripts\run_gsk_family.py work as they are, because each adds src/ to the import path itself. The python -m gsk_family.cli.* module forms do not, and neither do most other scripts that import gsk_family (for example the scripts\run_all_*.py and scripts\run_ablation.py launchers, papers\scripts\generate_ablation_matrix.py and generate_ablation_exhibits.py): they stop with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'gsk_family' unless src is on PYTHONPATH, so set it once per shell, from the repository root:

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt        # runtime only
python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt    # runtime + dev tooling
$env:PYTHONPATH = "src"                          # for python -m gsk_family.cli.* and the scripts\ launchers

Requires CPython >=3.10,<3.14. The runtime stack is NumPy, SciPy, pandas, matplotlib, PyYAML, and Numba (version ranges pinned in pyproject.toml).

Journal Revision Experiments (one command)

The five reviewer-requested experiments from the Algorithms revision: E1-E4 from the round-1 major revision (D-0047, CR-0023), plus E5, added in round 2 and pre-registered as Amendment A4 before it executed. The other six round-1 reviewer points needed no runs and are already applied.

Rehearse first — 20 seconds, and it verifies itself:

python scripts\run_revision_experiments.py --smoke

Runs every kind of leg through the identical code path at tiny scope (2 functions, 2 runs, one dimension, 3,000 evaluations), then checks that each leg actually wrote the rows it promised and prints SMOKE PASSED or SMOKE FAILED. Output goes to results/_revision_smoke/, which is gitignored and can never reach the campaign tree. Do not start the real run until this is green.

Then the real thing. This is the whole command:

python scripts\run_revision_experiments.py

Start it and leave it. It is resumable: after any interruption — Ctrl-C, a reboot, a crashed leg — re-run the identical line and it continues from the first incomplete cell instead of repeating finished work. Every leg is written overwrite: false.

LegReviewer pointWhat it runsRuns
E1R2.3Coordinate-basis final polish (the missing third arm)2,958
E2R1.3 / R2.2DT-GSK at the comparators' NP = 1005,916
E3R2.1Uniform vs tiered: the D=10 and D=100 parameter sets applied at every dimension11,832
E4R2.7Parameter sensitivity, 27 one-factor cells11,745
E5R2.7Dimension-boundary sensitivity, 4 executed cells (round 2, Amendment A4)1,740
Total34,191

E5 registers five boundary cells but runs four. The fifth — boundary 20 -> 31, i.e. the low-tier parameter set applied at D = 30 — is identical by construction to E3's uniform-low arm at D = 30 (51 runs per function), so it is reused from the promoted round-1 release rev-rel-2026-08-26-dd42d37eb rather than re-executed. E5's four executed cells use 15 runs per function, as E4 does.

Roughly 25–33 hours at 15 workers for E1–E4; E5's four cells add about five percent to that. Progress is printed and appended to results/_revision/driver.log, so a detached run can be followed with:

Get-Content -Wait results\_revision\driver.log

Useful variants:

python scripts\run_revision_experiments.py --smoke        # 20 s rehearsal, self-verifying
python scripts\run_revision_experiments.py --status       # progress table, runs nothing
python scripts\run_revision_experiments.py --dry-run      # the plan, runs nothing
python scripts\run_revision_experiments.py --only E1,E2   # a subset
python scripts\run_revision_experiments.py --only E5      # the round-2 leg alone
python scripts\run_revision_experiments.py --workers 8    # fewer workers

--smoke composes with the others, so --smoke --dry-run shows the rehearsal plan without running it.

The smoke run prints per-function comparisons against the reference bank that will look alarming — "Worse: 2", errors around 1e+09. That is expected and not a failure: 3,000 evaluations against the reference's 100,000–1,000,000. Judge the smoke by the SMOKE PASSED line, not by those tables.

Notes that matter:

  • Output is staged under results/_revision/, never benchmarks/. Promotion into an evidence release is a separate, deliberate step.
  • The driver pins OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS/NUMBA thread counts to 1 per worker. D >= 50 byte-stability depends on that; do not run the legs by hand without it.
  • E3's override dictionaries are generated programmatically from _dt_profiles.pub_overrides(). Eighty-eight config keys differ between the D=10 and D=100 tiers — never transcribe them.
  • E1 is driven by scripts/run_e1_basis_contrast.py, not by a YAML config. It needs the research hook research_oracle_basis, which the public adapter deliberately does not forward and which tests/regression/test_dormant_mechanisms_unreachable.py exists to keep unreachable from every config, profile, CLI and adapter path — that test also pins the adapter's source text, and dt_gsk.py is hash-gated by validate_provenance_claims.py. Expressing E1 as a config would break a regression test and a hash gate. The tripwire scans src/gsk_family only and its docstring records that reaching the hooks "requires a new evidence release", which is what E1 produces. Nothing under src/ is modified.
  • The pre-registration addendum is signed: papers/review_2026_08_24/revision_experiments_preregistration.md, dated 2026-08-25, before any result from these experiments existed. It records that §1.4 of papers/build_prompt_phases/phase_05/ablation_preregistration.md — which binds that a mechanism be verified ON in the baseline at a dimension before a disable delta is claimed there — does not govern E1 or E3, and registers replacement rules rather than reinterpreting it: E1 holds enablement constant and substitutes the basis, E3 is a configuration transplant with its own binding rule. E3 licenses only "the tiered configuration does / does not outperform a tier-constant one at dimension d"; no E3 cell may be attributed to a single subsystem. E4 is registered exploratory — descriptive only, no hypothesis tests and no corrected p-values. The addendum is append-only: two amendments dated 2026-08-26 record an E4 perturbation-level deviation at D=100 and a corrected E2 scope statement.

After The Campaign (promotion, analysis, exhibits)

The campaign of record is already through this chain. Run it in this order:

python papers/scripts/promote_revision_experiments.py --dry-run
python papers/scripts/promote_revision_experiments.py
python papers/scripts/analyze_revision_experiments.py
python papers/scripts/generate_revision_exhibits.py
  • Promotion writes the flat, manifest-bound tree benchmarks/cec_reference_results/_revision/ — release rev-rel-2026-08-26-dd42d37eb, 31 arms, 252 files, read-only — not the retired _releases/<release-id>/ layout. curves/ and per-session console logs are excluded by manifest, never silently dropped. Re-running against an existing tree verifies instead of re-copying, and adds only missing arms.
  • Analysis is strict-source: it reads the promoted tree plus the two frozen releases it pairs with, never results/. It mints the self-manifested bundle papers/analysis/rev-rel-2026-08-26-dd42d37eb/ and refuses to emit unless seed pairing verifies and its pinned known-answer battery reproduces.
  • Exhibits render SA05--SA08 — Supplementary Section S9, Tables A43--A46 — and their Word twins from that bundle, from the same plain data in both formats.

The release is additive and non-superseding: the primary release rel-2026-07-20-67d9345f9 is untouched and check_frozen_analysis still reads 115/115 byte-identical.

Full Paper Pipeline (in order)

The complete data-to-PDF sequence. --workers 15 is shown (matches configs/publish/); drop to the safe baseline 2 if memory-constrained (see Common Flags). Dependency order: §1 data -> §3 stats -> §5/§6 figures & tables -> §7 build; and §2 ablation -> §4 aggregate -> §6 table. The granular sections below this one give variants (tight-on-memory, reference-seed, per-optimizer, targeted). The numbered comments in the block below (1 to 8d) are pipeline stages, not Part 1's Steps; the "see runbook.md step 7" in papers/scripts/build_change_marked_pdf.py means stage 7 here (Build the PDFs).

# --- 1. Generate run data: the three benchmark campaigns ---
# Thread pinning is NOT optional at D >= 50. run.py pins nothing by itself
# (scripts/run_campaign.py sets the six variables below to 1, and
# scripts/run_revision_experiments.py sets five of them for its workers),
# and thread count sets floating-point reduction order in DT-GSK's Numba
# kernels, which --numba-threads 1 pins per worker, and in NumPy's BLAS/LAPACK
# calls (the eigendecomposition behind the final polish among them), which only
# the BLAS/OpenMP variables reach, and only when set before Python starts. An
# unpinned re-run is not comparable with a pinned one. It is NOT a promise that
# a pinned re-run reproduces archived bytes: D-0051 demonstrated the opposite
# across builds -- a pinned re-execution reproduced the transplant arm on all
# 26 divergent cells and the archive on none. Pin it so a run is comparable
# with itself.
# --overwrite rebuilds each optimizer's per_run.csv for the suite from scratch.
# After an interruption, re-run the same line WITHOUT it to resume; but an
# optimizer the interrupted run never reached still holds any earlier rows,
# which a resume keeps, so re-run that optimizer with --overwrite instead.
$env:OMP_NUM_THREADS=1; $env:MKL_NUM_THREADS=1; $env:OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1
$env:VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1; $env:NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=1; $env:NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=1
python run.py --root . --optimizer gsk,agsk,apgsk,fdb-agsk,atmals-gsk,egsk,dt-gsk --suite cec2017 --function 1:30 --dimension 10,30,50,100 --runs 51 --parallel --workers 15 --numba-threads 1 --convergence-graphs --overwrite
python run.py --root . --optimizer gsk,agsk,apgsk,fdb-agsk,atmals-gsk,egsk,dt-gsk --suite cec2011 --function 1:22 --dimension native --runs 25 --parallel --workers 15 --numba-threads 1 --convergence-graphs --overwrite
python run.py --root . --optimizer gsk,agsk,apgsk,fdb-agsk,atmals-gsk,egsk,dt-gsk --suite cec2013 --function 1:28 --dimension 10,30,50 --runs 51 --parallel --workers 15 --numba-threads 1 --convergence-graphs --overwrite

python scripts/run_all_cec2020.py --workers 15
python run.py --root . --optimizer gsk,agsk,apgsk,fdb-agsk,atmals-gsk,egsk --suite cec2013lsgo --function 1:15 --dimension native --runs 25 --parallel --workers 4 --numba-threads 1

python -m gsk_family.cli.stats --suite CEC2017 --dims 10,30,50,100
python -m gsk_family.cli.stats --suite CEC2011
python -m gsk_family.cli.stats --suite CEC2013 --dims 10,30,50

python papers/scripts/build_pdf.py

#     _word_ooxml.source_date_epoch() PREFERS an inherited SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH over

#     silently produces a non-reproducible DOCX that still passes every gate.

Remove-Item Env:FORCE_SOURCE_DATE -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$env:SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH = "1783641600"

python papers/scripts/build_docx.py --supplementary

python scripts/check_package_contents.py  # builds sdist+wheel from `git archive HEAD`
#     and fails if either carries the evidence bank, papers/, or withheld
#     material. Added 2026-08-29 after a setuptools upgrade started honoring the
#     old recursive package-data glob and produced a 1.2 GB wheel.

# --- 8c. Freeze re-mint, after any change to one of the 15 files tracked in
#     papers/governance/main_manuscript_freeze_manifest.json. Re-mint it
#     byte-surgically -- CRLF, 2-space indent, both `sha256` and `bytes`
#     updated per file -- and verify the json.dumps(indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
#     round-trip AND the trailing-byte convention against the ORIGINAL bytes
#     before rewriting; read_text()/write_text() normalize the line endings and
#     break every hash. Procedure of record:
#     docs/development/FINAL_PUBLICATION_PLAN.md (take the trailing bytes from
#     the file, not from that document -- this manifest does end with a
#     trailing CRLF) ---

# --- 8d. check_manifest hashes the WORKING TREE, not the committed blob, so a
#     re-saved binary can still pass 15/15. Close that blind spot by hand: each
#     size below must equal the `bytes` recorded for that file in the manifest ---
git cat-file -s HEAD:papers/DT-GSK.pdf
git cat-file -s HEAD:papers/DT-GSK.docx
git cat-file -s HEAD:papers/supplementary.pdf
git cat-file -s HEAD:papers/supplementary.docx
git cat-file -s HEAD:papers/cover_letter.pdf

Smoke Test

A few seconds: one optimizer, one function, a tiny evaluation budget. Use this to confirm the toolchain before launching a full sweep:

python run.py --root . --optimizer gsk --suite sphere --function 1 --dimension 4 --runs 1 --max-evaluations 80 --overwrite

Or run a packaged smoke campaign from YAML:

python run.py --root . --config configs/smoke.yml --output-root results/_smoke

The config runs one reduced-budget GSK CEC2017 cell (F1, D = 10, 1,000 evaluations) with overwrite: true and names results/_run_all/ as its output root. Keep --output-root results/_smoke: in the shared tree the run would rebuild results/_run_all/gsk/cec2017/summary/per_run.csv from that one run, and a later campaign run without --overwrite (such as scripts\run_all_cec2017.py) would keep its reduced-budget row as run 1 of F1 at D = 10, because resume matches function, dimension, run and seed only.

CEC2017 All Optimizers

Use a visible worker count in campaign commands. The safe baseline is --workers 2; increase the number only when you know the machine has spare CPU and memory and you are not running other heavy work. --convergence-graphs opts in to rendered PNG plots; omit it when you only need the convergence CSV files.

python run.py --root . --optimizer gsk,agsk,apgsk,fdb-agsk,atmals-gsk,egsk,dt-gsk --suite cec2017 --function 1:30 --dimension 10,30,50,100 --runs 51 --parallel --workers 2 --numba-threads 1 --convergence-graphs --overwrite

To resume after a crash or reboot, re-run the same line without --overwrite: runs already recorded are skipped. With it, the runner rebuilds each named optimizer's per_run.csv for the suite from this invocation alone, discarding every earlier row, not only the cells the command names (see Common Flags); this line names the whole suite, so nothing outside it is lost. The optimizers run one after another, so an optimizer the interrupted run never reached still holds whatever the tree held before, and a resume would keep it; re-run that optimizer with --overwrite instead. --numba-threads 1 keeps the D = 50 and D = 100 cells comparable (see Full Paper Pipeline step 1).

Other Full Sweeps

Benchmark backend defaults to auto, which uses the Python/Numba evaluator. Use --parallel --workers 2 as the safe baseline; raise 2 deliberately when the machine has enough headroom. Each line pins one Numba thread per worker, as the locked configs/family_*.yml campaigns do (numba_threads: 1), and recomputes its suite from scratch (resuming is covered under CEC2017 All Optimizers). The CEC2020 and CEC2013-LSGO lines write to results/_rerun/, because the tracked campaign staging for those two suites already lives in results/_run_all/ and --overwrite would rebuild it.

# CEC2020 - 10 functions, dims 5/10/15/20
python run.py --root . --optimizer gsk,agsk,apgsk,fdb-agsk,atmals-gsk,egsk,dt-gsk --suite cec2020 --function 1:10 --dimension 5,10,15,20 --runs 30 --parallel --workers 2 --numba-threads 1 --convergence-graphs --output-root results/_rerun --overwrite

# CEC2013 - 28 functions, dims 10/30/50
python run.py --root . --optimizer gsk,agsk,apgsk,fdb-agsk,atmals-gsk,egsk,dt-gsk --suite cec2013 --function 1:28 --dimension 10,30,50 --runs 51 --parallel --workers 2 --numba-threads 1 --convergence-graphs --overwrite

# CEC2011 - native per-problem dims
python run.py --root . --optimizer gsk,agsk,apgsk,fdb-agsk,atmals-gsk,egsk,dt-gsk --suite cec2011 --function 1:22 --dimension native --runs 25 --parallel --workers 2 --numba-threads 1 --convergence-graphs --overwrite

# CEC2013-LSGO - D=1000, very expensive; shown for one optimizer
python run.py --root . --optimizer gsk --suite cec2013lsgo --function 1:15 --dimension 1000 --runs 25 --parallel --workers 2 --numba-threads 1 --convergence-graphs --output-root results/_rerun --overwrite

CEC2013 Family Panel

CEC2013 is the second GSK-family comparison suite: 28 functions, dims 10/30/50, 51 runs (CEC2013 competition standard). Run the full 7-optimizer panel (note: egsk runs via the scipy-SLSQP port, and the statistical panel reads egsk from the committed scipy-SLSQP port CSVs, the comparator of record):

python run.py --root . --optimizer gsk,agsk,apgsk,fdb-agsk,atmals-gsk,egsk,dt-gsk --suite cec2013 --function 1:28 --dimension 10,30,50 --runs 51 --parallel --workers 2 --numba-threads 1 --convergence-graphs --overwrite

Tight on memory -- one optimizer at a time (repeat per optimizer id):

python run.py --root . --optimizer dt-gsk --suite cec2013 --function 1:28 --dimension 10,30,50 --runs 51 --parallel --workers 2 --numba-threads 1 --convergence-graphs --overwrite

The runs above land under results/_run_all/<optimizer>/cec2013/. Every committed panel CSV is unified-seed (each run_config.json records seed_policy: unified), so a --seed-policy reference run does not line up with them. That policy switches a comparator to its original implementation's own seed formula, for parity checks against that implementation, and leaves dt-gsk on the unified seed under every policy (see docs/reference/seed_policy.md). Give such a run its own output root, so its rows never mix with or replace the runs in results/_run_all/:

python run.py --root . --optimizer agsk --suite cec2013 --function 1:28 --dimension 10,30,50 --runs 51 --seed-policy reference --parallel --workers 2 --numba-threads 1 --output-root results/_reference_seed --overwrite

The CEC2013 family report (Friedman ranks, Nemenyi CD, pairwise Wilcoxon/Holm, effect sizes) reads every optimizer, dt-gsk included, from benchmarks/cec_reference_results/cec2013/, which carries all seven, so it reports the committed panel rather than the runs above (see Statistical Analysis to analyse your own runs):

python -m gsk_family.cli.stats --suite CEC2013 --dims 10,30,50

CEC2013 convergence-curve grids (28 functions at a chosen dimension; the script finds the panel whether it lands in benchmarks/cec_reference_results/cec2013/ or a reproduced-run tree):

python papers/scripts/generate_cec2013_convergence.py --dimension 30

The CEC2013 head-to-head (T11--T13) and Wilcoxon summary (T14) LaTeX tables are emitted by the shared table generator, which reads the promoted evidence at benchmarks/cec_reference_results/_paper_tables/ and never touches results/ staging:

python papers/scripts/generate_latex_tables.py

Config Launchers

Only run_all_cec2020.py runs a paper campaign (configs/family_cec2020.yml). run_all_cec2017.py and run_all_cec2011.py run configs/all_cec2017.yml and configs/all_cec2011.yml (five optimizers without egsk and dt-gsk, 25 runs, unpinned Numba threads). run_all_cec2013.py and run_all_cec2013lsgo.py are one-cell GSK smokes (F1, 1 run, 1,000 evaluations, --overwrite, written under results/). For the paper's settings use the commands in Part 1, Step 5. The launchers live in scripts/ (see scripts/README.md):

python scripts\run_all_cec2017.py
python scripts\run_all_cec2011.py
python scripts\run_all_cec2020.py
python scripts\run_all_cec2013.py
python scripts\run_all_cec2013lsgo.py

You can also drive campaigns directly from the YAML files in configs/:

python run.py --root . --config configs/all_cec2017.yml   # five-optimizer, 25-run template, not the paper's settings
python run.py --root . --config configs/all_optimizers_smoke.yml
python run.py --root . --config configs/all_optimizers_cec2017_reduced.yml

Common Flags

FlagEffect
--root .Project root; keeps the command portable across checkout locations.
--optimizer a,b,cComma-separated optimizer IDs to run.
--suite NAMEOne of the six suites.
--function 1:30 or --function 5Function range (lo:hi) or single ID.
--dimension 10,30,50,100 / nativeComma-separated dims; native uses each problem's intrinsic dimension (CEC2011).
--runs 51Independent runs per cell (CEC2017 convention is 51; CEC2011 commonly 25).
--max-evaluations NOverride the evaluation budget (used by smoke cells).
--parallel / --serialProcess pool vs single process; parallel is the default unless --serial.
--workers NBound concurrent processes (and peak memory). Safe baseline 2.
--convergence-graphs / --no-convergence-graphsRender PNG curves, or write curve CSVs only.
--numba-threads 1One Numba thread per worker process. run.py pins none by itself; keep it for DT-GSK at D >= 50 (see Full Paper Pipeline step 1).
--overwriteRebuild each named optimizer's per_run.csv for the suite from this invocation alone, discarding every earlier row, not only the named cells. Omit it to resume: recorded runs are skipped, matched on function, dimension, run and seed only (not budget or code version).
--seed-policy referenceUse the reference seed labels instead of the default unified schedule.
--statsStream per-dimension Wilcoxon + Friedman analysis live (opt-in; skips vanilla gsk; cec2011 reports via its per-suite rollup).

Tight On Memory

Run one optimizer at a time with the same safe worker baseline. After a crash, re-run the same line without --overwrite to resume: runs already recorded are skipped.

python run.py --root . --optimizer gsk --suite cec2017 --function 1:30 --dimension 10,30,50,100 --runs 51 --parallel --workers 2 --numba-threads 1 --convergence-graphs --overwrite
python run.py --root . --optimizer agsk --suite cec2017 --function 1:30 --dimension 10,30,50,100 --runs 51 --parallel --workers 2 --numba-threads 1 --convergence-graphs --overwrite
python run.py --root . --optimizer apgsk --suite cec2017 --function 1:30 --dimension 10,30,50,100 --runs 51 --parallel --workers 2 --numba-threads 1 --convergence-graphs --overwrite
python run.py --root . --optimizer fdb-agsk --suite cec2017 --function 1:30 --dimension 10,30,50,100 --runs 51 --parallel --workers 2 --numba-threads 1 --convergence-graphs --overwrite
python run.py --root . --optimizer atmals-gsk --suite cec2017 --function 1:30 --dimension 10,30,50,100 --runs 51 --parallel --workers 2 --numba-threads 1 --convergence-graphs --overwrite
python run.py --root . --optimizer egsk --suite cec2017 --function 1:30 --dimension 10,30,50,100 --runs 51 --parallel --workers 2 --numba-threads 1 --convergence-graphs --overwrite
python run.py --root . --optimizer dt-gsk --suite cec2017 --function 1:30 --dimension 10,30,50,100 --runs 51 --parallel --workers 2 --numba-threads 1 --convergence-graphs --overwrite

Need more speed? Increase the worker count deliberately:

python run.py --root . --optimizer gsk --suite cec2017 --function 1:30 --dimension 10,30,50,100 --runs 51 --parallel --workers 4 --numba-threads 1 --convergence-graphs --overwrite

Targeted Runs

A targeted run gets its own output root. With --overwrite in the shared results/_run_all/ tree it would rebuild that optimizer's whole per_run.csv from this one cell, discarding every other cell already recorded there.

# One optimizer, one function, one dimension
python run.py --root . --optimizer agsk --suite cec2017 --function 5 --dimension 30 --runs 51 --parallel --workers 2 --convergence-graphs --output-root results/_targeted --overwrite

# Same run with reference seed policy (a separate root again, so the two seed policies never mix)
python run.py --root . --optimizer agsk --suite cec2017 --function 5 --dimension 30 --runs 51 --seed-policy reference --parallel --workers 2 --convergence-graphs --output-root results/_targeted_reference_seed --overwrite

Results And Validation

Stats, summaries, seed schedules, metadata, and convergence curves are written under:

results/_run_all/<optimizer>/<suite>/

Validate imported reference evidence:

python -m gsk_family.cli.validate --references benchmarks/cec_reference_results

Compare generated results with imported references:

python -m gsk_family.cli.validate --compare results/_run_all/gsk/cec2017 benchmarks/cec_reference_results

Statistical Analysis

Paper-grade GSK-family comparison (Friedman ranks, Nemenyi CD, pairwise Wilcoxon/Holm, effect sizes); outputs land under results/_run_all/_analysis/<suite>/:

python -m gsk_family.cli.stats --suite CEC2017 --dims 10,30,50,100

Single source of truth. All paper statistics -- including the proposed dt-gsk -- are read from the committed reference panel benchmarks/cec_reference_results/<suite>/<optimizer>/ (flat layout: <optimizer>_<suite>_D<dim>.csv + per_run.csv + curves/ + gen_logs/). The convergence-figure generators (§5 of the pipeline) also read curves and gen_logs from there. For gsk-stats, a local reproduced run under results/_run_all/ is read only for the proposed optimizer, and only when the reference tree lacks that cell; it never reads comparators from results/. (The review pack below loads through result_loader.load_comparison_set, which falls back to results/ for any optimizer the reference tree lacks.)

Analysing your own runs. Because the committed panel is read first, a fresh run of a cell it already carries does not change the report. Build a panel folder in which your runs replace the committed files for the same optimizer and dimension (everything you did not run keeps the committed file), then point --reference-root at it; --out keeps the report apart from the default results/_run_all/_analysis/:

python scripts/build_stats_panel.py --suite cec2017 --results results/_run_all --out results/_own_panel
gsk-stats --suite cec2017 --reference-root results/_own_panel --out results/_own_panel/_analysis

Regenerating reference data (avoid the doubled-suite trap). The runner refuses any output_root equal to or inside benchmarks/cec_reference_results — ensure_output_root_allowed aborts at startup, because the reference tree is the frozen evidence base. Regenerate into a staging root under results/ and promote the vetted bundle with scripts/promote_evidence.py (promotion writes a versioned benchmarks/cec_reference_results/_releases/<release-id>/ subtree; it never rewrites the flat live <suite>/<optimizer>/ layout). The runner writes <output_root>/<optimizer>/<suite>/, so point output_root at the containing tree, not at a suite folder itself:

# correct -> results/_refresh_staging/<optimizer>/<suite>/...
python run.py --root . --config <cfg>.yml   # with output_root: results/_refresh_staging
# WRONG (creates <root>/cec2017/<opt>/cec2017/...):
#   output_root: results/_refresh_staging/cec2017

Stream the per-dimension Wilcoxon + Friedman analysis live during a run with the opt-in --stats flag (default off; it skips vanilla gsk — cec2011 is supported via its per-suite rollup):

python run.py --root . --optimizer dt-gsk --suite cec2017 --dimension 10 --dimension 30 --stats

Paper Review Pack

Build the advisor review PDF (matplotlib PdfPages, no LaTeX): a headline dashboard, 7-algorithm CEC2017/CEC2011 mean tables, and 7-algorithm GSK-family convergence grids. Missing convergence curves are logged, never fabricated.

python papers/scripts/generate_review_pack.py

Writes papers/DT-GSK-CEC2017-review.pdf (and ..._missing.log).

DT-GSK Diagnostics

Opt-in per-generation telemetry for root-cause analysis (default off; observational — it never changes RNG order, evaluations, or results). Enable it via optimizer_options.dt_diagnostics in a YAML config; one JSONL trace is written per cell under <output_root>/dt-gsk/<suite>/diagnostics/:

optimizers: [dt-gsk]
suite: cec2017
functions: [4, 13, 19, 26, 30]
dimensions: [10, 30, 50, 100]
runs: 5
seed: 20240620
seed_policy: unified
rand_generator: threefry
parallel: true
workers: 2
generation_logs: true
convergence_graphs: false
overwrite: true
output_root: results/_experimental/dt_diag
optimizer_options:
  dt_diagnostics: true
  dt_diagnostics_include_all_fields: true
python run.py --root . --config configs/experimental/dt_diag.yml
python scripts/analyze_dt_diagnostics.py --input results/_experimental/dt_diag/dt-gsk/cec2017/diagnostics --out results/_experimental/dt_diag/dt-gsk/cec2017/diagnostics_analysis

The analyzer writes diagnostics_summary.csv, wrong_basin_candidates.csv, and per-subsystem summaries (ACE entropy, linkage reliability, diversity, local-search ROI, boundary hits). Wrong-basin flagging is general — never hard-coded to a function.

DT-GSK Ablation (CEC2017)

The scaffold ablation isolates each DT-GSK mechanism on the full CEC2017 suite (F1, F3--F30; n = 25) by toggling optimizer_options -- every mechanism defaults to True in the locked profile, so a cell disables exactly one. The vendored ISM core is byte-identity locked; these options are the sanctioned, code-untouching way to configure it. SGSM stays disabled throughout the scaffold ablation -- the SGSM overlay is ablated separately (the CEC2013 hold-out, full / no-adaptive / no-sgsm cells), not here.

Mechanism toggles (set to false to disable that cell's component):

optimizer_options keyMechanism
ace_enabledACE knowledge control
psr_enabled / sp_nlpsr_enabled(NL)PSR population-size reduction
bse_enabled (bse_cauchy_enabled)Budget-Safe Escape (+ Cauchy rescue)
argp_enabledAcceptance-Rate Gated Pool Pruning
linkage_blockwise_enabledLinkage-aware block crossover
arch_enabledElite archive
local_search_enabledCoordinate endgame local search (local_search_method defaults to coordinate)
final_polish_enabledEigenframe final polish
interaction_graph_enabledSGSM interaction graph (off for this ablation)
deep_stall_restart_enabledDeep-stall full restart

The pipeline is three scripts: scripts/run_ablation.py writes one config per cell under configs/_ablation/ and runs each to its own output dir; generate_ablation_matrix.py rolls the cells up into the mean-Friedman-rank matrix; generate_ablation_exhibits.py renders the supplement tables.

# inspect the per-cell configs without running
python scripts/run_ablation.py --dimension 30 --dry-run

# run the default cell set (baseline + one disable-one cell per mechanism), n=25
python scripts/run_ablation.py --dimension 30 --runs 25 --workers 2

# or only a subset
python scripts/run_ablation.py --only baseline,no_linkage,no_bse

# aggregate the cells -> results/ablation/ablation_matrix_rank_summary_cec2017_D30.csv
python papers/scripts/generate_ablation_matrix.py --suite cec2017 --dimension 30

# render the scaffold-ablation supplement tables (SA01/SA02) -> papers/tables/SA01.tex, SA02.tex (\input in the supplement)
# (reads the manifest-verified frozen release copy, not the fresh results/ablation/ aggregate)
python papers/scripts/generate_ablation_exhibits.py

Per-cell output lands under results/_ablation/<cell>/dt-gsk/<suite>/. The default set is the baseline (full scaffold, SGSM off) plus one disable-one cell per mechanism; edit the CELLS dict in scripts/run_ablation.py to match the full 16-cell design. Some mechanisms have paired flags (e.g. psr_enabled vs sp_nlpsr_enabled, bse_enabled vs bse_cauchy_enabled) -- confirm the exact semantics in src/gsk_family/optimizers/_dt_profiles.py before finalizing the matrix.

Preview the enabled/disabled matrix for every cell without running:

python scripts/run_ablation.py --dry-run          # remove-one (default)
python scripts/run_ablation.py --mode add-one --dry-run

--mode picks the ablation direction: remove-one (default) disables one mechanism from the full scaffold; add-one enables one from bare GSK (the ATMALS-GSK-style "enable one, keep the rest at base" design).

Match ATMALS-GSK's protocol with --suite (two suites) and, if you want its exact direction, --mode add-one. ATMALS-GSK evaluated on CEC2017 (51 runs) and CEC2011 (25 runs); run the ablation on both:

# CEC2017 ablation at the main-study run count (51)
python scripts/run_ablation.py --suite cec2017 --dimension 10,30,50,100 --runs 51 --workers 15
# CEC2011 ablation (native dims; --dimension ignored)
python scripts/run_ablation.py --suite cec2011 --runs 25 --workers 15
python papers/scripts/generate_ablation_matrix.py --suite cec2011

Note: SGSM activates only at D >= 50, and CEC2011's native problem dims vary widely, so the CEC2011 ablation mostly probes the scaffold mechanisms rather than the SGSM overlay -- state that scope in the paper.

The parameter-sensitivity study is a separate experiment, not ablation evidence. It is E4 of the round-1 revision campaign: 27 one-factor cells at D=30 and D=100, n = 15, promoted inside rev-rel-2026-08-26-dd42d37eb and reported as Table A46 (exhibit SA08). It is registered exploratory -- descriptive only, no hypothesis tests and no corrected p-values. The older results/dt-gsk/sweeps/parametric-study/ tree (n = 3) that T21/T22 would have come from is absent from this repository; that gap is EG-006 in papers/governance/evidence_gap_register.md, whose "omit" branch was exercised -- T21/T22 were never committed and the manuscript never cites them.

Slow Or Crashing

If a campaign is thrashing memory or a worker keeps dying, step down the concurrency before giving up on parallelism entirely:

python run.py <args> --parallel --workers 2    # safe baseline
python run.py <args> --serial                  # single process, slowest but most robust

The default process backend self-heals: if a worker dies mid-run the pool is rebuilt and the affected work is retried, falling back to serial for a cell that still cannot complete -- so a run finishes rather than hanging. For CEC2017 composition cells (F21-F30) automatic process runs retain an upper memory-safety cap of 8 workers; an explicit --workers N is treated as your chosen speed/memory tradeoff.

Avoid --parallel-backend thread for real campaigns. Calling the parallel Numba kernels from many Python threads can deadlock, and the threaded path does not scale for these GIL-bound loops. Use the default process backend, or --serial.

Quality Checks

python -m pytest -q                                   # full test suite
python -m pytest tests\smoke\test_documentation_commands.py -q   # doc-path + command smoke
python -m ruff check .                                # lint
python scripts\validate_profile_lock.py --root .      # profile-lock validation
python scripts\build_docs_html.py                     # rebuild the HTML doc site

Freeze-Pass Cycle (the passes-49..52 recipe)

Any edit to a hash-gated file (the 15 freeze files or the 2 hashed sources) voids the current pass and takes a full cycle. The order below is the one that worked four times in a row; deviations are where the recorded incidents live.

  1. Edit sources; rebuild the gated renders they feed. Main PDF: python papers/scripts/build_pdf.py; DOCX: build_docx.py (+ --supplementary if supplementary.tex changed); supplement PDF: build_supplementary.py. Cover letter: pdflatex x2 in papers/ under SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1783468800 FORCE_SOURCE_DATE=1, then build twice and byte-compare (it must be deterministic).
  2. Commit the APPLY. The marked PDFs and the change register diff v2.13..HEAD (committed refs, not the working tree), so they can only be rebuilt AFTER this commit: build_change_marked_pdf.py --doc main / --doc supplementary, then build_change_register.py — read the passage count it prints and sync it wherever it is quoted if it moved.
  3. Mint the freeze manifest (papers/governance/main_manuscript_freeze_manifest.json, CRLF): byte-surgical text replacement, never json.dump; update sha256+bytes per changed file, generated_utc, anchor_commit = the apply commit, and the phase text. check_manifest.py must then read 15/15 AND sources 2/2.
  4. Update the package manifest (submission_package_manifest.json, CRLF): sha256, bytes, pages, version id, note, authoritative_commit. After writing, re-verify sha AND bytes against disk — the pass-51 updater's size needle silently never matched and left stale byte counts that no gate checks (found and fixed in pass-52).
  5. Run the 13-gate ladder twice (section 8b above plus profile-lock).
  6. File the governance pair (next free CR-xxxx / D-xxxx — verify free at apply time), sync the status banners (REVISION_STATUS, CLAUDE.md, papers/PAPER_REVIEW_PROMPT.md), commit the close.
  7. Bump CITATION.cff BEFORE cutting the tag (no leading v in the cff version; the tag-before-bump mistake was made twice and is caught by validate_citation_cff.py), then tag vN.NN and push main + tag.

The reviewer-facing response letter is untracked (D-0049) and outside the freeze; its exact rebuild command — with the load-bearing Ligatures=NoCommon, HyphenChar=None and letter-specific epoch — is recorded in papers/submission/SUBMISSION_KIT.md. Sweep phrase-level policies against the RENDER (pdftotext), never only the source: line-wrapped phrases defeat source grep (pass-51 lesson).
